pages.markdown:
## Springs of the Eastern Ridge

## 1. Field notes

The survey team walked the eastern ridge in the first week of May. They recorded each spring, its flow in litres per minute, and the colour of the water. Most springs ran clear. Two ran brown after rain and cleared again within a day.

The survey team walked the eastern ridge in the first week of May. They recorded each spring, its flow in litres per minute, and the colour of the water. Most springs ran clear. Two ran brown after rain and cleared again within a day.

## 2. Equipment

Each team carried a hand pump, a set of sample bottles, a notebook and a small scale. The scale drifted by a few grams over the week, so the team checked it against a reference weight every morning.

Each team carried a hand pump, a set of sample bottles, a notebook and a small scale. The scale drifted by a few grams over the week, so the team checked it against a reference weight every morning.

## 3. Results

The ridge holds forty-one springs. Thirty-six of them flow all year. The five seasonal springs sit on the south slope, where the soil is thin and the rock is close to the surface.

The ridge holds forty-one springs. Thirty-six of them flow all year. The five seasonal springs sit on the south slope, where the soil is thin and the rock is close to the surface.

## 4. Next steps

The team will return in October to measure the same springs at the end of the dry season. They will also map the two brown springs and look for the source of the silt.
